context: The prompt requests adding auto-save functionality to the Technical Design Schema Editor, removing save buttons. However, this contradicts the previous prompt P-019 where manual save was explicitly chosen (Q5, option A) to maintain consistency with the existing editor workflow and allow batch changes before persisting. This questionnaire clarifies the desired auto-save behavior and how to handle conflicts with the existing workflow.

questions.question-text: Should auto-save completely replace the manual save button or work alongside it?

options.label: Replace - Remove save button, only auto-save
options.pros: Simpler UI, no user action needed, automatic data persistence, modern UX pattern
options.cons: No way to discard changes, harder to batch multiple edits, no confirmation before save, conflicts with P-019 decision

options.label: Hybrid - Auto-save but keep save button for manual control
options.pros: Safety net with manual save option, allows batch edits, user control over when to persist
options.cons: Confusing UX (two save mechanisms), may be redundant, unclear when to use which

options.label: Replace with undo/redo - Auto-save with undo/redo functionality
options.pros: Modern pattern, allows mistake correction, no save button needed, automatic persistence
options.cons: Complex to implement, requires change history tracking, significant scope increase

questions.recommendation-rationale: The prompt explicitly states 'There should be no need of save buttons', indicating complete replacement with auto-save. This provides the cleanest UX and matches the stated requirement, despite conflicting with P-019's manual save decision.

options.label: On every change (immediate)
options.pros: Maximum data safety, no data loss possible, instant persistence
options.cons: Many server requests, performance impact, harder to batch edits, validation errors interrupt workflow

options.label: Debounced after inactivity (e.g., 2 seconds after last change)
options.pros: Balances safety and performance, allows typing/editing without interruption, fewer server requests
options.cons: Slight delay before save, possible data loss in 2-second window, requires debounce logic

options.label: On blur/navigation (when leaving field or switching items)
options.pros: Natural save points, completes logical edit units, fewer saves than immediate
options.cons: Data loss if browser crashes during editing, may miss some changes, less obvious when save happens

questions.recommendation-rationale: Debounced auto-save (2-3 seconds) provides the best balance between data safety and user experience. It allows users to complete their thoughts while typing without triggering saves on every keystroke, while still providing near-immediate persistence.

questions.question-text: How should validation errors be handled with auto-save?

options.label: Block auto-save until validation passes
options.pros: Ensures data integrity, prevents saving invalid schemas, catches errors early
options.cons: Interrupts workflow with error messages, may prevent saving partial work, frustrating for users

options.label: Save anyway, show validation warnings
options.pros: Doesn't interrupt workflow, allows saving work-in-progress, user can fix errors later
options.cons: May save invalid schemas, could break schema loading, data integrity concerns

options.label: Save locally, validate before server save
options.pros: Preserves work locally, validates before actual persistence, catches errors without losing edits
options.cons: Complex implementation, requires local storage, may confuse users about save state

questions.recommendation-rationale: For a development tool like the schema editor, allowing auto-save of work-in-progress is more important than strict validation. Users can fix validation errors before using the schema. This prevents frustration from blocked saves while editing.

questions.question-text: Should there be visual feedback when auto-save occurs?

options.label: Show save indicator (e.g., 'Saving...' then 'Saved')
options.pros: Clear feedback to user, confirms data persistence, builds trust in auto-save
options.cons: May be distracting, adds visual clutter, needs UI space

options.label: Silent auto-save (no feedback)
options.pros: Cleaner UI, no distractions, seamless experience
options.cons: User uncertainty about whether changes are saved, no confirmation of persistence

options.label: Minimal feedback (small icon or status bar only)
options.pros: Subtle confirmation, doesn't interrupt workflow, provides reassurance
options.cons: Easy to miss, may not be noticed by users

questions.recommendation-rationale: Users need confidence that their changes are being saved automatically. A clear 'Saving...' / 'Saved' indicator in the status bar provides reassurance without being intrusive. This is especially important when removing the manual save button.

questions.question-text: What happens to the backup functionality with auto-save?

options.label: Keep backup button, create backup before each auto-save
options.pros: Maximum safety, can recover from any auto-save, preserves backup feature
options.cons: Many backup files, storage bloat, may slow down auto-save

options.label: Keep backup button, manual backups only
options.pros: User control over backups, prevents backup bloat, backups remain intentional
options.cons: Auto-saves not backed up, can't recover from automatic save errors

options.label: Remove backup button, periodic auto-backups (e.g., hourly)
options.pros: Automatic backup safety net, no user action needed, time-based recovery points
options.cons: Loss of manual backup control, may not backup before critical changes

questions.recommendation-rationale: Keep the manual backup button for intentional backup creation (e.g., before major changes). Creating backups on every auto-save would generate too many files. This balances safety with practicality.

questions.question-text: Should the reload button behavior change with auto-save?

options.label: Keep reload button, no unsaved changes warning (since auto-save)
options.pros: Consistent with auto-save model, no false warnings, cleaner UX
options.cons: May reload after unsaved changes if auto-save hasn't triggered yet, potential data loss in edge cases

options.label: Keep reload button with warning if changes pending auto-save
options.pros: Protects against data loss, warns if debounce timer active, safety net
options.cons: May show warnings even with auto-save active, potentially confusing

options.label: Remove reload button (not needed with auto-save)
options.pros: Simplifies UI, removes confusion, auto-save makes reload less useful
options.cons: No way to reset to saved state, useful feature removed

questions.recommendation-rationale: With auto-save active, the reload button can simply reload without warnings. The debounce delay is short enough that the risk is minimal. This provides a clean way to refresh the editor state from the file.
